Our Report's Cover
This year’s Integrated Annual Report, 
“Where Strategy Meets Evolving 
Healthcare Needs, Science & 
Sustainability,” reflects Granules India’s 
continued transformation into a science 
led, globally competitive pharmaceutical 
company. The cover symbolises 
our purpose of improving lives by 
responding to changing healthcare 
needs through innovation, quality and 
sustainable growth.
The rising sun represents new 
possibilities, while the family walking 
together reflects our commitment 
to patients, communities and future 
generations. It also signifies the balance 
between scientific progress, responsible 
business practices and long term 
value creation.
The report highlights our progress 
in expanding complex generics, 
strengthening regulatory excellence, 
advancing peptide therapeutics, 
enhancing manufacturing capabilities 
and embedding sustainability across our 
operations. Together, these milestones 
demonstrate how strategy, science and 
sustainability come together to shape 
the future of healthcare and create 
lasting value for all stakeholders.

About the Report
We are pleased to present the Integrated 
Annual Report of Granules India Limited 
for FY 2025-26. This Report provides 
a comprehensive overview of how 
we continue to drive value creation 
across our pharmaceutical value chain, 
while advancing sustainable, ethical 
and responsible growth. The Report 
reflects our continued commitment to 
transparency, governance and resilience 
in an evolving global environment. 
Our Reporting Framework 
This Report has been prepared in 
accordance with the guiding principles 
of the International Integrated 
Reporting Framework (IIRC) developed 
by the International Integrated 
Reporting Council (IIRC). It explains 
how sustainability and operational 
excellence are embedded in our 
business model to create long-term 
value for all stakeholders. The statutory 
disclosures align with applicable 
regulatory and financial reporting 
requirements, including:  
 
 
The Companies Act, 2013  
 
 
Indian Accounting 
Standards (Ind AS)  
 
 
SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 
 
 
Secretarial Standards issued by ICSI 
Forward-looking Statements
This Report contains certain forward-
looking statements regarding Granules 
India’s future performance, strategy 
and outlook. Words such as ‘expects’, 
‘intends’, ‘plans’, ‘believes’, ‘may’, ‘will’, 
and other similar expressions are used 
to denote such statements. These are 
based on present assumptions and 
involve risks and uncertainties. Actual 
results may differ materially.  
Reporting period, frequency 
This Integrated Report covers the 
reporting period of FY 2025-26 (1st April 
2025-31st March 2026) and is published 
on an annual basis, in alignment with the 
company’s financial reporting cycle.
All disclosures in this report have 
been made with reference to the GRI 
Standards and UNGC principles, and 
are aligned with the company’s financial 
reporting cycle.

External Assurance 
This Integrated Report has undergone 
external assurance for FY 25-26. The 
assurance was conducted by Bureau 
Veritas (India) Pvt. Ltd for the full fiscal 
year, and We verified the reliability and 
accuracy of our data following GRI 
guidelines, using specific assumptions 
and methodologies outlined in the 
Report. Details of the assurance level 
and the type of assurance obtained are 
provided in the respective sections. The 
GRI has also been notified regarding 
the application of its standards in 
preparing this Report.
Feedback 
Granules is committed to transparency 
and stakeholder engagement, and 
we consider feedback an essential 
part of improving our disclosures. 
For any queries or suggestions 
related to this report or our ESG 
performance, stakeholders are 
encouraged to contact us at   
investorrelations@granulesindia.com.
You can also reach us by submitting 
your queries through our contact form at  
https://granulesindia.com/contact-us/.
Reporting Scope and Boundary  
This Report covers the operations 
of Granules India Limited, including 
its domestic and international 
manufacturing facilities, R&D centres, 
and marketing offices. Information 
pertaining to subsidiaries and joint 
ventures is included wherever relevant. 
Any exceptions or exclusions are clearly 
stated in the respective sections
The disclosures and performance related 
to environmental and social indicators 
covered under Human Capital, Social 
and Relationship Capital, and Natural 
Capital , as well as the Business 
Responsibility and Sustainability Report 
(BRSR), are presented on a standalone 
basis for Granules India Limited. Key 
environmental and social performance 
information related to the Company’s 
subsidiaries is disclosed separately in 
the relevant sections of this report.

In an industry defined by constant evolution, 
meaningful progress is shaped by the ability to 
anticipate change, respond with agility and create 
solutions that remain relevant in a rapidly transforming 
healthcare landscape. At Granules India, we continue 
to strengthen our role in advancing healthcare by 
combining scientific expertise, integrated capabilities 
and responsible growth to create meaningful impact 
across global markets.
From integrated generics to high-
entry-barrier products, we are 
building a robust portfolio designed 
for scale, resilience and long-term 
value creation. Our focus remains on 
strengthening capabilities, fostering 
confidence and enabling our people to 
translate knowledge into meaningful 
outcomes across functions, operations 
and partnerships.
As one of the few Indian pharmaceutical 
companies with integrated capabilities 
across APIs, PFIs and Finished 
Dosages, we recognise the growing 
importance of global partnerships 
in strengthening healthcare supply 
chains and expanding access to 
quality medicines. From our integrated 
pharmaceutical platform to strategic 
acquisitions that combine Swiss 
expertise with robust manufacturing 
scale in India, we continue to deepen 
collaborations with partners and peers 
across the world to collectively shape 
the future of healthcare. This strategic 
expansion is also strengthening our 
participation in specialised therapeutics 
and higher-value opportunities, enabling 
us to build a more diversified and 
future-ready pharmaceutical business.
We believe that innovation driven by 
science and guided by purpose is 
fundamental to delivering safe, effective 
and high-quality medicines that people 
can trust. Our efforts remain focused 
on strengthening healthcare systems 
through the consistent and reliable 
supply of essential medicines, while 
continuing to build responsibly through 
operational excellence, sustainable 
practices and long-term value creation 
embedded across our operations.
We believe transformation becomes 
inevitable when opportunity meets 
determination. Rooted in the belief that 
healthcare is a responsibility, especially 
towards those who cannot afford it, 
this philosophy continues to shape our 
approach towards responding to evolving 
healthcare needs, advancing innovation 
with purpose and creating sustainable 
impact for communities, healthcare 
systems and stakeholders worldwide.

About Us
Advancing Healthcare 
through Science, Scale and 
Integrated Excellence
Granules India offers a diverse and continually evolving portfolio to 
the global pharmaceutical market, spanning Active Pharmaceutical 
Ingredients (APIs), Pharmaceutical Formulation Intermediates (PFIs), 
Finished Dosages (FDs) and Peptides CDMO products. Guided by science 
and a clear focus on advancing high-value, specialised therapies, our 
teams are committed to delivering safe, effective and affordable medicines 
that meet the expectations of partners and patients across geographies.
This integrated capability enables a seamless journey from concept to market, underpinned by rigorous 
compliance at every stage of development and production. Our large-scale manufacturing platform, strong 
regulatory framework and process-driven approach enable us to advance global healthcare, we are taking 
a deliberate step towards strengthening localised partnerships and shaping sustainable value creation.

Management’s Message
Dr. Krishna Prasad Chigurupati
Chairman & Managing Director
Granules has returned to 
a clear growth trajectory, 
anchored in a structural 
reset of the portfolio toward 
complex, differentiated 
products and disciplined 
execution across our core 
operating platforms.
Dear Shareholders,
The world of healthcare is being reshaped by forces that are 
both challenging and full of promise. Aging populations, the 
rising burden of chronic and lifestyle diseases, expanding 
access to treatment across emerging economies and the 
growing need for affordable medicines continue to support 
long-term growth in global pharmaceutical demand. At the 
same time, the operating environment is becoming more 
complex. Pricing pressures in mature generics markets, rising 
regulatory expectations, and supply chain realignment are 
accelerating the shift towards complex generics, specialty 
products and value-added manufacturing.
India is well-positioned within this evolving global order. 
Built on decades of manufacturing scale, scientific capability 
and regulatory expertise, the Indian pharmaceutical industry 
continues to strengthen its role in global healthcare delivery. 
India’s pharmaceutical exports crossed US$31 billion in FY26 
despite global headwinds, underlining both the resilience of the 
increased to 43% from 31%, demonstrating tangible progress 
in our strategy to build a more differentiated and higher-
quality earnings base.
Finished dosages remain the core of our business, with North 
America continuing to anchor revenue and Europe emerging 
as a high-growth market, reflecting our intent to build a more 
geographically diversified growth model over time.
Our portfolio outlook is increasingly exciting, with a growing 
pipeline of complex generic opportunities, including potential 
first-to-file (FTF), Day 1 and Day 181 opportunities in high-
value areas such as CII (controlled substances) products 
and oncology. Our R&D pipeline has deepened considerably, 
with a growing proportion of filings directed toward complex 
generics. Applications from our Gagillapur facility, pending site 
clearance, represent a further pipeline of near-term value as 
the facility completes its regulatory journey. More broadly, our 
continued investments in R&D are creating visible optionality 
for the future.
A New Growth Engine
The acquisition of Senn Chemicals AG in Switzerland, 
completed during the year, marked our entry into the peptide 
CDMO space, a segment we believe holds significant 
long-term promise.
Senn brings decades of scientific expertise in peptide 
synthesis and longstanding customer relationships across the 
pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries. This is a deliberate 
step into an area of global therapeutics where scientific 
capability, manufacturing precision and long-term partnerships 
will increasingly define value creation.
Within the first year of acquisition, the business demonstrated 
encouraging momentum, turning EBITDA-positive in the 
Q4FY26 of the year and establishing itself as our fourth 
revenue pillar.
On the India side, our Peptides Platform, anchored by a new 
Centre of Excellence at IIT Hyderabad, is engaged in customer 
programmes in close collaboration with our Zurich team. 
Together, this provides us with a differentiated platform that 
combines Swiss scientific capability with Indian scale.
Our capacity expansion programme is being executed in 
a calibrated manner across both geographies, balancing 
growth ambitions with operational and financial prudence. 
We are strengthening our capabilities to participate in the 
rapidly expanding peptide therapeutics market, including 
GLP-1 therapies, which we view as an attractive long-
term growth avenue.
Where Ambition Meets Responsibility
Sustainability has become an increasingly important 
determinant of long-term competitiveness in the 
pharmaceutical industry, influencing market access, 
stakeholder expectations and capital allocation. Our purpose 
of healing lives responsibly through pioneering green science 
is supported by SBTi-validated targets aligned with the 
1.5°C pathway and our commitment to achieve net zero 
emissions by 2050.
During FY2025–26:
 
 
We earned an EcoVadis Gold rating, placing us among the 
top 5% globally.
 
 
We received a CDP Climate Change score of ‘A’.
 
 
The Gagillapur facility achieved Zero Waste to Landfill 
Platinum Plus certification.
 
 
We became a signatory to the UN Women’s 
Empowerment Principles.
 
 
Our S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment score 
improved to 62, positioning us within the top 10% globally.
These outcomes reflect the growing maturity of our 
sustainability journey and reinforce our standing as a 
responsible partner in global pharmaceutical supply chains.
Priorities for FY2027 and Beyond
Granules enters FY2027 materially better positioned than a 
year ago, with:
 
 
A stronger balance sheet , reflected in Net debt to 
EBITDA of 0.34x
 
 
A healthier pipeline anchored toward a complex and 
differentiated product portfolio
 
 
Improved compliance infrastructure
Our priorities for the year ahead are clear:
1.	
Complete the regulatory journey at Gagillapur.
2.	
Commercialise and utilise the capacity of the GLS 
Genome Valley facility across global regulated markets.
3.	
Continue accelerating our transition toward complex and 
differentiated products.
4.	
Drive the Peptide CDMO platform toward 
sustainable profitability.
Capital investments for the year ahead are planned across 
manufacturing, technology and supply chain infrastructure, 
with discipline and demand linkage guiding every 
allocation decision.
External uncertainties—including raw material cost pressures, 
logistics dynamics and a fluid geopolitical environment—will 
require careful navigation. We do not underestimate these. 
But we face them from a position of greater strength, greater 
clarity and greater organisational confidence than we have 
had in some time.
FY2025–26 was a year of one in which Granules returned to a 
stronger growth trajectory, anchored in portfolio discipline and 
improved execution. The progress was deliberate, necessary 
and foundational. As we step into the next phase, we carry with 
us the conviction that the platform we have built is becoming 
increasingly differentiated, resilient and capable of delivering 
sustainable long-term value.
On behalf of the Board and the entire Granules family, I 
express my sincere gratitude to our shareholders, customers, 
employees, partners, regulators and communities for their 
continued trust in us. We remain steadfast in our commitment 
to quality, compliance and responsible growth, while continuing 
to create enduring value for all our stakeholders.
Warm regards,
Dr. Krishna Prasad Chigurupati
Chairman & Managing Director
sector and the growing role of Indian companies in regulated 
and emerging markets alike. This is a responsibility that 
Granules India embraces with conviction.
It is within this context that we present our Integrated Annual 
Report for FY2025–26. We believe enduring value is created 
where strategy aligns with evolving healthcare needs, science 
translates ambition into innovation, and sustainable values 
guide responsible growth. This intersection continues to shape 
our decisions, our investments and our transition toward a 
more differentiated, science-led pharmaceutical platform.
A Year of Deliberate Reset and Measurable 
Progress
FY2025–26 was a landmark year for Granules India. We 
crossed the ₹50,000 million revenue milestone, delivering total 
revenue of ₹53,656 million, a growth of 20% year-on-year. 
EBITDA grew 25% to ₹11,851 million. Profit after tax stood at 
₹5,950 million, up 19% year-on-year.
Gross margins reached a record 65%, representing a structural 
expansion of approximately 1,500 basis points since FY2022, 
driven by a deliberate shift in portfolio mix toward complex 
and differentiated products. Importantly, this performance 
reflects more than operating leverage; it points to a structural 
strengthening of the business as our mix moves steadily up 
the value chain.
These results were delivered against a backdrop of elevated 
remediation expenditure, increased logistics costs and 
ongoing regulatory engagement, making the performance all 
the more meaningful. Six consecutive quarters of sequential 
revenue growth underscore that the progress we are seeing 
is increasingly structural and reflects a stronger, more resilient 
business foundation.
Strengthening the Foundation
Throughout FY2025–26, we maintained an uncompromising 
focus on quality and regulatory compliance, viewing 
compliance not as an episodic requirement, but as an 
institutional capability that must be continuously strengthened.
At our Gagillapur facility, we made significant progress on 
remediation, completing all key corrective actions on schedule 
and submitting our responses to the USFDA within stipulated 
timelines. Our engagement with the regulator remained 
constructive and transparent throughout. As we enter FY2027, 
we do so with the site audit-ready, remediation substantially 
complete and confidence in a positive outcome.
Beyond Gagillapur, we made significant regulatory progress 
across our manufacturing network, with 6 of our 8 facilities 
holding a clean EIR position and recent positive outcomes at 
GLS and GCH Packaging further strengthening our credibility in 
regulated markets.
Our US operations at GPI continued their strong trajectory, with 
the company moving to the 27th position among all US generic 
pharmaceutical companies by sales value, up from 74th in 
FY2021, and establishing a leadership position in the controlled 
substances space.
Moving Up the Value Chain

is now clearly reflected in our financial results. During FY26,

Industry Dynamics 
Shaping Strategic 
Priorities
The pharmaceutical industry is being 
increasingly shaped by sustainability 
expectations, regulatory scrutiny and the 
need for resource-efficient operations. At 
the same time, there is growing focus on 
responsible supply chains and climate-
conscious infrastructure development, 
aligning long-term business resilience 
with broader environmental stewardship 
and global sustainability commitments. 
In this context, Granules India is 
strengthening its operational and 
manufacturing capabilities to align with 
emerging sustainability priorities and 
strengthen its preparedness for evolving 
operational requirements.
India’s position as the “Pharmacy of the World” 
is underpinned by a distinctive combination 
of affordable pricing and assured quality, 
which has made Indian medicines widely 
preferred across global markets. This strength 
is further reinforced by manufacturing scale, 
cost competitiveness and robust capabilities 
in generic medicines, supported by effective 
government initiatives. The industry is also 
witnessing a gradual shift towards differentiated 
formulations, specialty products, complex 
generics and innovation-led CDMO offerings.  
India’s pharmaceutical sector continues to 
expand its global footprint through rising 
exports and steady foreign investment, 
reflecting strong international confidence in its 
manufacturing and regulatory standards.
The pharmaceutical industry is witnessing a 
growing shift towards complex formulations, 
and next-generation drug delivery systems. 
This shift is driven by increasing need for 
personalized, targeted, and long-term 
compliance therapies. Pharmaceutical 
companies are continuously innovating 
to meet the demand for products which 
are technologically advanced, clinically 
differentiated, and capable of addressing 
chronic and lifestyle-driven diseases 
more effectively.
The peptide therapeutics and CDMO 
segment are at the forefront of driving this 
shift, attracting heightened industry interest, 
supported by developments across fast 
growing obesity, diabetes, oncology, and other 
chronic therapy segments. These innovations 
are driving greater need for specialized 
development and manufacturing capabilities.

Business Overview
From APIs to an Integrated 
Pharma Platform 
As Indian pharma pivots towards innovation and sustainability, we at Granules 
India are charting a strong growth path driven by R&D and global ambitions 
amid evolving supply chain dynamics. We have evolved from an API-focused 
organisation into an integrated pharmaceutical company with capabilities 
across APIs, PFIs, finished dosages and peptide CDMO operations. Over time, 
we have strengthened our position across the pharmaceutical value chain as 
an innovation-led manufacturer.
Our core portfolio comprises products such as Paracetamol, Metformin, Ibuprofen and controlled substances, complemented 
by a future pipeline increasingly centred on innovation-led and technology-driven offerings supported by enzyme-based and 
continuous manufacturing platforms. This includes oncology therapies, large molecules, differentiated dosage formats such as 
liquids and nasal sprays, as well as peptide-based therapies strengthened through our CDMO capabilities.

Risk Management 
Enhancing resilience in a 
dynamic global environment
At Granules India Limited, risk management is a core pillar of 
governance and a strategic enabler of long‑term value creation. 
Operating in a highly regulated, evolving technological and global 
pharmaceutical ecosystem, the Company recognises that risks and 
opportunities are dynamic and increasingly interlinked across financial, 
operational, regulatory, technological and sustainability dimensions for 
value preservation and creation. Our enterprise-wide risk management 
(ERM) framework is designed to identify current and emerging risks and 
opportunities early, assess their potential impact, and embed mitigation 
actions into strategic and operational decision making and resilience.
Risk registers are reviewed quarterly, with enterprise risks escalated to the Board for deliberation. This structured cadence ensures 
continuous monitoring, accountability and timely intervention.
Risk Governance and Oversight
Risk oversight at Granules is driven 
at the highest level of governance. 
The Board of Directors provides 
strategic supervision, supported by 
the Risk Management Committee 
(RMC) constituted in accordance with 
SEBI (LODR) Regulations. The RMC 
is responsible for reviewing the risk 
management policy, overseeing the ERM 
framework and monitoring exposure 
across financial, operational, regulatory, 
technological, sectoral, talent, 
geopolitical and ESG-related risks.
Risk governance is further strengthened 
through a layered structure comprising:
 
 
Board and Board-level Committees 
for strategic oversight,
 
 
Internal Risk Committee (IRC) 
hereafter referred to as “Enterprise 
Risk and Resilience Committee” 
(ER2C) for operational coordination,
 
 
Designated Risk Owners 
across functions and 
manufacturing locations.

Occupational Health and 
Medical Surveillance
Employee health is supported through a comprehensive occupational health 
framework implemented across all locations. Fully equipped Occupational 
Health Centres are staffed by qualified medical professionals and supported 
by round-the-clock nursing teams, providing employees with access to timely 
medical care and emergency support.
01
Occupational Health Infrastructure
A structured medical surveillance programme enables proactive monitoring 
of employee health and occupational risks. Every new employee undergoes 
a detailed pre-employment medical examination to establish baseline health 
parameters and assess fitness for assigned roles.
This is followed by annual health assessments for all employees, while 
individuals working in high-risk areas undergo half-yearly medical examinations 
to facilitate closer monitoring and early identification of occupational health 
concerns. These assessments support informed decisions relating to job 
rotation, workplace controls and preventive healthcare measures.

Preventive Health Monitoring
Occupational Health Centres also promote preventive healthcare through 
health awareness programmes, counselling support and early diagnosis 
initiatives. All medical records are maintained with strict confidentiality 
and managed through secure systems accessible only to authorised 
medical professionals.

Case Study
Turning Data into Action: Safety Risk 
Intelligence Dashboard (SRID)
To strengthen proactive risk 
management and elevate safety 
performance across operations, 
we implemented the Safety Risk 
Intelligence Dashboard (SRID), 
a digital platform that converts 
safety observations into real-time 
actionable insights.
At the centre of the platform is a 
dynamic Safety Heat Map that 
enables leadership teams to visualise 
safety trends, compare performance 
across locations and identify 
emerging risks before they escalate.
The dashboard captures observations 
across categories including electrical 
safety, mechanical integrity, 
chemical handling, PPE compliance, 
housekeeping and pipeline leakages. 
Observations are classified according 
to risk severity, enabling teams 
to prioritise actions and allocate 
resources effectively.
A key strength of the platform lies in 
its ability to identify recurring safety 
hotspots and support targeted 
interventions. Integrated Corrective 
and Preventive Action (CAPA) 
tracking further strengthens 
accountability and ensures timely 
closure of actions.
By providing real-time visibility 
into safety performance, SRID 
supports a shift from reactive 
incident management towards 
predictive risk intelligence and 
preventive intervention.

him to pursue long-term career prospects while continuing to 
support his family.

family faced significant financial hardship. With her mother taking 
up tailoring work and the family relying partly on farming for income, 
continuing her education became increasingly challenging despite 
her strong academic performance. After completing her intermediate 
studies with 87%, she was introduced to Pharma Pathashala by her 
village head. Determined to support her family and build financial 
independence, Supriya embraced the opportunity to gain practical 
skills and create a more secure future.

Climate and Environment
Our approach to climate stewardship is centred on reducing greenhouse gas 
(GHG) emissions through energy efficiency, cleaner energy adoption and value 
chain decarbonisation. Guided by a structured transition roadmap, we are 
advancing actions across Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions to advance 
our sustainability commitments and support a resilient, low-carbon future.
Climate Action Transition Plan
Reducing Direct Emissions
We are improving energy efficiency across 
manufacturing operations through process 
optimisation, lower-carbon fuels and targeted emission 
reduction initiatives.
Scope 1
Addressing Indirect Emissions
We are increasing the use of renewable energy 
through captive power arrangements and renewable 
electricity procurement to reduce emissions from 
purchased power.
Scope 2
Driving Value Chain 
Decarbonisation
We are engaging suppliers, advancing green chemistry 
practices and developing lower-impact technologies to 
reduce emissions across our value chain and support 
broader industry decarbonisation efforts.
Scope 3
Science-Based Targets initiative (SBTi) Validation
Granules India received validation from SBTi for its near- and 
long-term greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets, aligned 
with the 1.5°C pathway. This milestone affirms the credibility of 
our decarbonisation roadmap and reinforces our commitment 
to delivering measurable climate action across our operations 
and supply chain.
Granules India's Net 
Zero Commitment 
and Emissions 
Reduction Goals
Net Zero Commitment
Achieve net zero GHG emissions across the value 
chain, including subsidiaries, by FY50.
Near-Term Targets
Reduce absolute Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions 
by 42% by FY30 from the FY23 baseline and 
transition to 100% renewable electricity by FY30.
Long-Term Goals
Achieve a 90% reduction in Scope 1, 2 and 3 
emissions by FY50.
What is SBTi? 
The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) is a globally 
recognised collaboration between CDP, the United Nations 
Global Compact, the World Resources Institute (WRI) 
and the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF). It enables 
companies to set GHG emissions reduction targets that 
are in line with the goal of limiting global warming to 1.5°C 
above preindustrial levels. SBTi provides clear, science-
aligned pathways to help companies translate climate 
ambitions into actionable plans.

Life Cycle Assessment
Granules uses Life Cycle Assessment 
(LCA) to evaluate the environmental 
impacts of its products across their 
life cycle, from raw material extraction 
and transportation to manufacturing 
and processing. By providing a 
comprehensive understanding 
of resource consumption and 
environmental interactions, LCA helps 
identify significant impact areas, quantify 
environmental burdens, and support 
data-driven decisions to enhance 
product sustainability.
During the year, the Company 
conducted LCA and Product Carbon 
Footprint (PCF) studies for three key API 
products—Paracetamol, Guaifenesin, 
and Metformin—through an independent 
external agency using specialized LCA 
modelling software. The assessments 
were carried out using a cradle-to-gate 
approach in accordance with ISO 14040 
and ISO 14044 (Life Cycle Assessment) 
and ISO 14067 (Product Carbon 
Footprint) standards.
The studies evaluated 13 environmental 
impact categories, including climate 
change, acidification, eutrophication, 
and ecotoxicity, providing valuable 
insights into product-level environmental 
performance. The assessments 
considered relevant life cycle stages 
within the defined system boundaries 
and utilized a combination of primary 
operational data and secondary life 
cycle inventory datasets sourced from 
recognized databases.
The findings help quantify environmental 
impacts across the product life cycle, 
identify environmental hotspots, and 
support informed decision-making for 
sustainability improvement initiatives. 
Detailed technical reports have been 
prepared and are maintained by 
the Company for internal reference, 
customer requirements, and 
stakeholder engagement.
Reducing GHG Emissions through 
Operational Improvements
During FY26, we implemented a series 
of initiatives aimed at enhancing energy 
performance, optimising processes 
and increasing the use of renewable 
power across our facilities. These efforts 
delivered measurable reductions in 
energy consumption and greenhouse 
gas emissions while improving 
operational effectiveness.
Energy efficiency measures included 
the replacement of conventional AHU 
motors with EC+ blowers, induction 
sealing fans with BLDC fans and 
the installation of energy-efficient 
air compressors, resulting in energy 
savings of 14,56,484 kWh. Additional 
gains of 7,60,290 kWh were achieved 
through process enhancement 
initiatives such as chiller and RT pump 
interlocks, compressed air pressure 
optimisation and the installation of 
temperature controllers.
We also expanded renewable energy 
generation through the installation of 
rooftop solar panels at the MUPS block 
in Gagillapur, generating 1,203 MWh of 
solar power. Complementary initiatives, 
including auto tube cleaning systems 
for chillers, automatic capacitor banks 
and energy-efficient lighting solutions, 
contributed to improved facility 
performance and resource utilisation. 
In addition, progress was achieved 
through the purchase of 80,000 MWh of 
Renewable Energy Certificates and the 
procurement of 7,286 MWh of renewable 
electricity under Power Purchase 
Agreements. Together, these measures 
helped avoid 61,973 tCO2e of emissions. 
Collectively, these initiatives resulted in 
annual energy savings of 23,09,552 kWh 
and annual GHG emission reductions 
of 64,467 tCO2e.
Site-Level Performance
Gagillapur Unit
Bonthapally Unit
The Gagillapur facility played a key role in advancing site-level resource 
performance through a combination of renewable energy deployment and 
equipment modernisation initiatives. Key initiatives included rooftop solar 
generation, renewable electricity procurement through PPAs, installation of 
energy-efficient EC+ blowers, deployment of high-efficiency air compressors 
and compressed air optimisation. Collectively, these measures delivered 
energy savings of 15,48,078 kWh and reduced emissions by 6,984 tCO2e of 
emissions during the year.
At Bonthapally, efforts were directed towards improving utility reliability 
and enhancing process effectiveness across critical operations. Initiatives 
included the replacement of AHU blowers, chiller and RT pump interlocking, 
temperature controller installation, air compressor upgrades and refrigeration 
system enhancements. Together, these measures generated energy savings 
of 758,830 kWh and reduced emissions by 538.7 tCO2e.
Ozone Depleting Substances
We remain focused on minimising the use of ozone-depleting substances 
across our cooling and air-conditioning systems through the phased 
transition to more environmentally responsible refrigerants. In alignment with 
the objectives of the Montreal Protocol, R-22 refrigerants are being replaced 
with alternatives such as R-134A and R-410, which have lower ozone 
depletion potential. During FY26, ozone-depleting substance emissions were 
limited to 0.007 MT in CFC-11 equivalent, reflecting our ongoing efforts to 
modernise refrigeration systems and reduce impacts on the atmosphere.
In FY26, we successfully avoided 
over 64,467 tCO2e emissions 
through a combination of energy 
efficiency measures, renewable 
energy procurement and 
operational optimisation.
These outcomes support our 
science-based targets and reinforce 
our commitment to Net Zero.

Our sustainability governance framework provides 
structured oversight of climate-related risks 
and opportunities.
 
 
A three-tier governance structure supports 
effective climate oversight, comprising the Board 
Sustainability and CSR Committee, a management-
level implementation team and plant-level teams 
responsible for execution and monitoring.
 
 
Our climate strategy is anchored by our commitment 
to achieve net zero emissions by 2050.
 
 
We have assessed both physical and transition 
climate risks across our operations in line with TCFD 
recommendations.
 
 
Climate scenario analysis has been undertaken 
across manufacturing facilities using IPCC 
pathways, including RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5, to 
evaluate potential climate impacts and strengthen 
resilience planning.
 
 
Investments in our greenfield facility and Granules 
CZRO support the development of environmentally 
responsible products and lower-carbon 
manufacturing pathways.
 
 
Climate-related risks are integrated into our 
Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework, 
enabling systematic identification, assessment and 
mitigation of climate and ESG risks.
 
 
We have aligned our climate risk assessment 
approach with TCFD recommendations and 
undertake periodic risk mapping exercises through 
internal risk committees.
 
 
During the year, we initiated a comprehensive 
assessment of climate and water-related risks using 
the TCFD framework.
 
 
We track climate-related risks and opportunities 
through defined targets and performance indicators.
 
 
Our Climate Action Transition Plan outlines initiatives 
focused on green molecules, green chemistry and 
sustainable manufacturing practices to strengthen 
climate resilience.
 
 
The Granules Climate Commitment establishes clear 
goals for emissions reduction, renewable energy 
adoption and enhanced climate transparency across 
Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions.
Our Focus
As climate-related challenges become increasingly complex, we are enhancing our risk assessment and monitoring capabilities 
to strengthen organisational preparedness and support effective decision-making. Our efforts are focused on evaluating climate 
risks and opportunities across multiple scenarios, including business-as-usual, transition and net-zero pathways. We are also 
broadening the scope of our analysis across supplier networks to gain deeper insights into potential business continuity impacts 
and emerging areas of strategic importance.
We recognise that managing air emissions is particularly critical in the pharmaceutical sector, where complex 
chemical processes can contribute to volatile organic compounds (VOCs), particulate matter, and combustion-
related emissions. We have established a comprehensive emission control framework across our facilities, 
supported by advanced pollution abatement technologies and rigorous monitoring mechanisms. Key interventions 
include the deployment of scrubbers, condensers, and bag filters, along with continuous emission monitoring 
systems (CEMS) that provide real-time visibility into emission performance. In addition, process optimisation 
and solvent recovery initiatives have helped minimise fugitive emissions and improve overall environmental 
performance. These measures support cleaner operations and help maintain high standards of environmental 
management across our manufacturing network.

and formulation to cooling, cleaning and utility operations. Given its critical role across manufacturing processes, effective 
water management is fundamental to maintaining operational reliability and resource efficiency.
Growing concerns around water stress, changing rainfall patterns and increasing scrutiny of pharmaceutical residues 
in aquatic ecosystems have heightened the importance of responsible water use and wastewater management across 
the industry. These challenges require organisations to adopt practices that balance operational requirements with the 
protection of shared water resources.

FY 25-26 reflected steady progress in enhancing resource productivity while supporting growing operational requirements. Total 
water withdrawal stood at 3,98,308 KL, with the majority sourced through third-party water supply arrangements. During the year, 
the introduction of grey water utilisation (3,060 KL), along with rainwater harvesting (1,457 KL), contributed to a more diversified 
sourcing profile. Notably, no surface water or groundwater was withdrawn across operations.
Total water consumption was 2,39,951 KL. Despite higher production volumes 
and an increase in overall consumption, water intensity improved to 4.16 KL/MT 
from 4.33 KL/MT in the previous year, demonstrating more efficient utilisation 
relative to output.
Wastewater generation increased to 1,58,357 KL, reflecting higher levels of 
manufacturing activity. Of this, 61,972 KL was recovered for reuse across 
operations. Although the recycling rate moderated to 39% due to higher 
wastewater volumes, the total quantity of water recovered remained broadly stable, 
highlighting the effectiveness of established recovery and treatment systems.
The year also saw progress in broadening alternative water sources, maintaining 
recovery levels and improving resource productivity, reinforcing our efforts to 
optimise water use across manufacturing operations.

With increasing global and national focus on

Neutrality refers to a balance between water 
withdrawal and replenishment, ensuring 
no net depletion of water resources due 
to operations. Demonstrating progress 
in this area will significantly enhance our 
environmental stewardship, regulatory 
compliance, and stakeholder confidence.
Granules has embarked on a structured 
journey towards achieving its water 
neutrality goal of becoming water positive 
Principles of Water Neutrality: The 3M-7R framework
Granules is aligning its water stewardship strategy with the 3M -7R framework outlined in the NITI Aayog 
Guidelines for Achieving Water Neutrality in Indian Industry. The 3M principles Map, Monitor, and Measure 
--form the foundation of this approach by enabling systematic assessment of water resources, continuous 
monitoring of water consumption and discharge, and the implementation of data-driven water management 
practices across operations.
Complementing this framework, the 7R principles Reduce, Recycle, Recover, Replenish, Recharge, 
Rejuvenate, and Recognize/Respect --guide comprehensive actions to optimize water use, enhance 
circularity through reuse and recycling, and promote watershed sustainability through groundwater recharge 
and ecosystem restoration initiatives.
By integrating the 3M and 7R principles, Granules is adopting a holistic and structured approach to improve 
water-use efficiency, strengthen water resilience, mitigate water-related risks, and advance its journey towards 
water neutrality and its long-term goal of becoming water positive by 2032.

Advancing Water Neutrality 
Through Source Diversion at 
Gagillapur
As part of our Water Neutrality Strategy, the 
Gagillapur site has implemented a source 
diversification initiative to reduce dependence on 
freshwater resources and enhance water circularity. 
Under this initiative, RO permeate from the CETP-
JETL (Common Effluent Treatment Plant) is utilized 
as make-up water for the cooling tower, replacing 
a portion of the freshwater previously used in 
utility operations.
This initiative has enabled a reduction of 
approximately 3,926 KL of freshwater consumption 
within a two-month period, demonstrating the 
effectiveness of treated wastewater reuse in driving 
sustainable water management. By redirecting 
treated water streams to utility applications, the site 
has improved resource efficiency while significantly 
lowering its freshwater footprint.
The project is a key contributor to our Water 
Neutrality journey, supporting our broader objective 
of reducing freshwater withdrawal through 
source diversification, water reuse, and circular 
water management practices. It also serves as 
a scalable model that can be replicated across 
other manufacturing locations, strengthening 
organization-wide water stewardship and resilience.

Hazardous waste is either sent to authorised Treatment,

enables partial energy recovery.

Granules BRSR - Executive Summary
Granules is committed to responsible business practices and sustainable 
growth, with a purpose of ‘Healing lives responsibly through pioneering 
green science’. Our Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report outline 
our dedication to environmental stewardship, social responsibility, and 
robust governance, while showcasing our accomplishments and outlining 
our future goals. 
KEY HIGHLIGHTS:
●	
Achieved the CDP Climate Change A List in 2025, advancing from C to B to A over three cycles.
●	
Earned CDP ratings of B and B- in its first-time Water Security and Forests disclosures.
●	
Received a “Gold rating” in our first corporate-level assessment by EcoVadis, placing us in the top 
5% of all rated companies globally across all industries with an overall score of 79/100 and a 97th 
percentile rank, this recognition is huge impetus to our strong commitment to sustainable, ethical, 
and responsible business practices.
●	
Achieved an A List rating in CDP’s Supplier Engagement Assessment (SEA) 2025, demonstrating 
strong leadership in engaging its supply chain on climate action.
●	
Achieved an S&P Global ESG Score of 62 out of 100.
●	
Gagillapur and Bonthapally Unit–I facilities are officially recognized as Water Neutrality Aspiring 
Plants by the CII–Triveni Water Institute (CII–TWI) for completing baseline and watershed delineation 
studies, as well as identifying community intervention opportunities, supporting Granules’ 2032 
water neutrality goal.
●	
Gagillapur unit has achieved Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWTL) Certification with Platinum + Rating with 
over 99% waste diversion rate from Landfill.
●	
Achieved Sedex Supplier Plus certification, demonstrating strong performance across social, 
environmental, and responsible sourcing parameters within its supply chain.
●	
Honoured with the Sustainability Award at Haleon’s Winning Together -Supplier Summit 2026, 
recognizing its measurable progress in environmental sustainability and commitment to responsible 
pharmaceutical manufacturing.
●	
Granules received the Silver Award at the CII National EHS Excellence Awards 2025 for its Gagillapur 
Unit and Granules Life Sciences site, while Unit-I Bonthapally and Unit-IV Visakhapatnam were 
recognized with the Bronze Award during the same ceremony.
●	
Become an official signatory to the UN-WEP (UN Women-UN Global Compact Women’s 
Empowerment Principles), reaffirming its commitment to gender equality and alignment with SDG5 
(Gender Equality).
●	
Joined the Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Initiative (PSCI) as an official Supplier Partner, reinforcing 
its commitment to ethical, responsible, and sustainable supply chain practices.
●	
Retained its membership with the UNGC (United Nations) Global Compact, reaffirming its 
commitment to the 10 principles of human rights, labour, environment, and anti-corruption.
●	
Became a member of the British Safety Council (BSC) and the National Safety Council (NSC), 
reinforcing its commitment to workplace health and safety.
●	
Published our inaugural Integrated Annual Report in FY 2024-25, aligned with the GRI Standards 
and the UN Global Compact (UNGC) principles.
●	
Our Net Zero target by 2050, approved by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), is aligned with 
the 1.5°C pathway.
Our Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report demonstrates our commitment to the nine principles of the National 
Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (“NGRBC”) as well as our progress against the stated objectives across 
environmental, social and governance (“ESG”) parameters.
The BRSR disclosures are in terms of Regulation 34(2)(f) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations 2015 and consist of three sections:
•	
Section A provides a broad overview of the business, its offerings, business and operations footprint, employees, related 
parties, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and transparency.
•	
Section B covers management and process disclosures related to the businesses aimed at demonstrating the structures, 
policies and processes put in place towards adopting the NGRBC Principles and Core Elements.
•	
Section C provides essential, and leadership indicator-wise disclosures mapped to the nine principles of NGRBC.

Granules India Limited (GIL) is a distinguished pharmaceutical company specializing in the production of Active 
Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API), Pharmaceutical Formulation Intermediates (PFI), and Finished Dosages (FD) products. 
Since its establishment in 1991, the company has successfully expanded into key international pharmaceutical markets, 
including the United States of America, Canada, Latin America, Europe, Asia Pacific, and India.
	
	
Renowned for its innovative processes and exceptional efficiencies, Granules India Limited supplies a diverse range 
of over 60 molecules and pharmaceutical products to more than 300 customers across 80 countries. The company 
maintains a strong global presence with offices strategically located in India, the United States, and the United Kingdom.
	
	
Granules India Limited operates six state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities, with four located in Hyderabad, Telangana, 
and two in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. These facilities hold regulatory approvals from esteemed agencies such

international quality standards.
	
	
Granules is a preferred supplier of superior quality pharmaceutical products for the world's leading branded pharma 
and generics companies, as well as to the top retailers in developed markets. Exports now contribute over 92% of the 
Company’s revenue.

Energy
 
 
Granules continue to demonstrate a growing commitment to sustainable energy practices. In FY26, 
renewable energy consumption increased by nearly 72%, rising from 213.24 TJ in FY25 to 366.30 
TJ. This shift resulted in 37% of the total energy (Coal + Electricity) being sourced from renewables 
(Biofuel, Renewable power), a significant step forward in our decarbonization journey. 
 
 
% of Renewable Energy share of consumed Electricity is 98% in FY26 which is notably increased from 
base year where it was 9.8% in FY23.
 
 
Despite an increase in overall energy consumption (from 881.18 TJ to 990.10 TJ), the increase in 
renewable share reflects our active transition toward cleaner energy sources, including biofuels and 
renewable electricity. 
 
 
Notably, energy intensity (TJ per MT of production) declined from 0.0176 TJ in FY25 to 0.0172 TJ in FY26.
Emissions
 
 
Since our base year (FY23), we have achieved a 45.7% reduction in total Scope 1 and Scope 2 
(market-based) emissions; bringing it down from 112,571 tCO2e in FY23 to 61,136 tCO2e in FY26. This 
includes an 19.8% drop compared to the previous year alone.
 
 
This remarkable progress is driven by our increasing use of renewable energy and energy-efficient 
operations. One of the key steps we took was installing a 1 MW on-site solar power system at our 
Gagillapur unit, which is now contributing to our clean energy supply.
 
 
While our direct emissions (Scope 1) remained almost constant, we made significant progress in 
reducing our electricity-related emissions (Scope 2). Market-based Scope 2 emissions dropped 
sharply from 56,306 tCO2e in FY23 to 1285 tCO2e in FY 26, showing our shift towards greener 
electricity sources.
Water
 
 
Specific water consumption improved from 4.33 KL/MT in FY25 to 4.16 KL/MT in the current year, 
reflecting enhanced operational efficiency.
 
 
39% of the wastewater generated is recycled, reinforcing our commitment to sustainable water 
management and circular practices.
Waste
 
 
Around 83% of the hazardous waste is disposed of by cement industries for co-processing, thereby 
promoting circular economy as well as reducing the GHG footprint.
 
 
100% of our non-hazardous waste generated at our operations are recycled through authorized vendors

At Granules India Limited, sustainability remains deeply embedded in our business philosophy and strategic direction, anchored 
in our purpose of “Healing lives responsibly through pioneering green science.” During the reporting period, we continued to 
strengthen our Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance, while proactively responding to evolving regulatory 
frameworks, stakeholder expectations, and operational challenges.
	
Granules India Limited achieved inclusion in the CDP Climate Change ‘A List’ (2025), marking a consistent progression from C 
to B to A over three disclosure cycles and reflecting strong climate governance and performance. The Company also expanded 
its environmental disclosures by participating in CDP’s Water Security and Forests assessments for the first time, securing 
ratings of B and B-, respectively.
	
We are pleased to have secured an ‘A List’ rating in CDP’s Supplier Engagement Assessment (SEA) 2025), reflecting our strong 
commitment to embedding climate accountability across our supply chain and actively engaging suppliers in sustainability 
aligned practices.
	
Additionally, our S&P Global ESG Score of 62 (out of 100) provides independent validation of our performance across

ensuring environmental compliance, and promoting responsible and sustainable operations, thereby strengthening 
stakeholder trust and organisational resilience.

Granules has implemented robust Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to enable employees and workers to effectively 
identify, report, and mitigate work-related hazards. A structured safety observation and interaction programme is in place

monitoring and management of workplace risks.
	
	
Comprehensive occupational health and safety training is provided to all employees and workers, covering hazard 
identification, risk assessment methodologies, and appropriate mitigation measures. These programmes ensure a strong 
understanding of workplace risks and reinforce proactive safety practices.
	
	
Emergency preparedness is strengthened through regular evacuation drills, where employees are trained in the use of 
critical safety equipment, including fire hydrants, firefighting systems, spill and leak control mechanisms, and alarm 
systems. These initiatives equip employees with the knowledge and confidence to report hazards promptly and respond 
effectively to potential emergencies.
	
	
Granules also ensures active integration of contractors into EHS communication frameworks, including safety meetings, 
awareness programmes, and training initiatives. EHS awareness is further reinforced through the use of visual boards, 
digital displays, posters, and video-based communication across facilities. The Company fosters a culture of openness by 
encouraging employees and contractors to report concerns and suggest improvements without fear of retaliation, thereby 
strengthening overall safety governance and continuous improvement.

Describe the processes for identifying key stakeholder groups of the entity.
	
Granules identifies key stakeholder groups through a systematic process that involves assessing and understanding 
the individuals, organizations, or entities that significantly impact or are impacted by our operations and decisions. Our 
approach includes:
 
 
Stakeholder Mapping: We conduct stakeholder mapping exercises to identify and prioritize groups based on their influence,

Describe the internal mechanisms in place to redress grievances related to human rights issues? 
	
Granules has established robust internal mechanisms to effectively address grievances related to human rights issues. 
Employees and stakeholders are encouraged to report any concerns regarding human rights violations through multiple 
channels, including direct communication with their managers, the Head of the Department, the Unit HR Manager, or the 
Compliance Officer. 
Raising Concern
As a standard practice, we encourage individuals to discuss or report any concerns regarding potential 
violations with their manager. If someone is uncomfortable reporting to their supervisor, they can raise 
their concern with the Head of the Department, Unit HR Manager, or Compliance Officer.
Reporting Violation
Employees are encouraged to promptly report any potential or actual violations of laws, company policies, 
or the Code of Conduct to their Manager/Supervisor, Unit HR, CFO, CHRO, or Compliance Officer.
Investigation
The Code of Business Conduct Committee will promptly and thoroughly investigate every concern and 
report of violation as per applicable law and procedures.
Disciplinary Action
Based on the nature and particulars of the violation, the investigation committee recommends corrective 
and preventive action, including disciplinary action.
No Retaliation
We strictly prohibit retaliation against individuals who report alleged violations in good faith. Our Policies 
ensures that employees can raise concerns without fear of reprisal, fostering a culture of transparency 
and accountability
	
Upon receiving a grievance, Granules follows structured procedures outlined in our policies, ensuring confidentiality and 
sensitivity throughout the investigation. We prioritize prompt and impartial handling of grievances to uphold our commitment 
to ethical conduct and respect for human rights. Our goal is to resolve issues swiftly and appropriately, fostering a workplace 
environment where human rights are safeguarded and respected.
	
At Granules, we follow a staged process in addressing human rights issues:
	
Whistleblower Policy:
	
We have devised an effective whistleblower mechanism enabling employees to freely communicate their concerns about 
illegal or unethical practices. The Company has also established a vigil mechanism for employees to report concerns about 
any unethical behaviour, actual or suspected fraud or violation of the Company’s code of conduct. The prime objective of this 
policy is to provide employees and Directors an avenue to raise concerns in line with the commitment of Granules to the highest 
possible standards of ethical, moral, and legal business conduct and its commitment to open, fearless, genuine concern 
communication. The pre-eminent intention of this policy is to provide necessary safeguards for the protection of employees 
from reprisals or victimization for whistleblowing in good faith.
	
Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy (POSH):
	
As per the requirement of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition & Redressal) Act, 2013 
(‘POSH Act’) and rules made thereunder, our Company has formed an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) for its workplaces to 
address complaints about sexual harassment under the POSH Act. We have a detailed policy for preventing sexual harassment 
at the workplace, which ensures a free and fair inquiry process with clear timelines for resolution.

Does the entity have any project related to reducing Green House Gas emissions? If yes, then provide details.
	
During FY 2025–26, Granules India Limited undertook focused energy conservation, efficiency improvement, and renewable 
energy initiatives across its manufacturing sites, delivering measurable environmental and financial benefits. The Company 
achieved total energy savings of 2,309,552 kWh, resulting in a GHG emission reduction of 1,640 tCO2e through energy 
efficiency measures. Further, increased adoption of renewable electricity contributed to an additional 6,027 tCO2e reduction 
in Scope 2 emissions. Additionally, for offsetting emissions, Granules procured 80,000 MWh of I-RECs for its API, FD, and 
R&D units, resulting in a reduction of approximately 56,800 tCO2e of GHG emissions. Collectively, these initiatives generated 
annual cost savings of approximately ₹176.4 lakhs, and the avoided GHG emissions is 64,467 tCO2e strengthened energy 
resilience, and supported alignment with statutory disclosures and ESG reporting requirements under BRSR, GRI, and global 
rating frameworks.

The Gagillapur unit was the major contributor to energy and emissions performance through a combination of renewable energy 
adoption and system efficiency improvements. Key initiatives included rooftop solar generation of 1,203 MWh, procurement of 
7,286 MWh renewable electricity through PPA, replacement of conventional AHU blowers with energy efficient EC+ blowers, 
installation of a high efficiency air compressor, and compressed air pressure optimization. These measures resulted in energy 
savings of 1,548,078 kWh, GHG reduction of 1,099 tCO2e from efficiency initiatives and 5,885 tCO2e from renewable electricity, 
along with annual cost savings of ₹111.6 lakhs.
	
At the Bonthapally unit, energy optimization efforts focused on HVAC systems, utilities, and process efficiency. Key measures 
included replacement of AHU blowers with energy efficient Aeronaut blowers, interlocking of chillers and RT pumps, installation 
of temperature controllers in cleanroom AHUs, deployment of IRIS controllers for air compressors, and installation of an auto 
tube cleaning system for refrigeration units. These initiatives delivered energy savings of 758,830 kWh, corresponding to a GHG 
reduction of 538.7 tCO2e, and annual cost savings of ₹64.6 lakhs.
	
Energy conservation initiatives at the Parawada unit-IV included replacement of conventional street lighting with energy 
efficient bollard lights, adoption of BLDC motors for canteen sealing fans, and automation of capacitor banks to achieve 
unity power factor. These measures resulted in energy savings of 2,644 kWh, GHG reduction of 2 tCO2e, and annual cost 
savings of ₹0.5 lakhs.
	
These initiatives underscore the Company’s commitment to sustainability through operational excellence, renewable energy 
adoption, and continuous improvement in energy use, all aligned with its long-term Net Zero ambitions and science-based targets.

10.	 Briefly describe the waste management practices adopted in your establishments. Describe the strategy adopted by 
your company to reduce usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your products and processes and the practices 
adopted to manage such wastes.
	
Granules operate in a sector producing significant amounts of hazardous and non-hazardous waste. Our manufacturing 
facilities generate substantial amounts of solvents and other hazardous waste, which we aim to reduce through process 
optimization and co-processing initiatives. Under our clean manufacturing practices, all solid wastes from our plants are either 
co-incinerated in cement industries or handled by authorized vendors.
	
Our Waste Management systems and processes are guided by ISO 14001. We segregate hazardous and non-hazardous 
waste at the source and store them in dedicated areas within our facilities. After thorough sorting, hazardous waste is stored 
by category in designated hazardous waste storage areas and disposed of at Pollution Control Board-approved facilities in 
compliance with relevant regulations.
	
We registered with CPCB under the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) under the Importers category in the current 
reporting period, and our waste management plan is aligned with the EPR guidelines. 
	
100% of the non-hazardous waste generated at our manufacturing sites is sent to authorized recyclers for recycling. 
Approximately 83% of our hazardous waste undergoes energy recovery through co-processing, and the rest is disposed 
of through Authorized vendors. These measures ensure we manage waste responsibly, mitigate environmental impact, and 
adhere to regulatory requirements effectively.

If the entity has undertaken any specific initiatives or used innovative technology or solutions to improve resource

During FY 2025–26, Granules India Limited undertook focused energy conservation, efficiency improvement, and renewable 
energy initiatives across its manufacturing sites, delivering measurable environmental and financial benefits. The Company 
achieved total energy savings of 2,309,552 kWh, resulting in a GHG emission reduction of 1,640 tCO2e through energy 
efficiency measures. Further, increased adoption of renewable electricity contributed to an additional 6,027 tCO2e reduction 
in Scope 2 emissions. Additionally, for offsetting emissions, Granules procured 80,000 MWh of I-RECs for its API, FD, and 
R&D units, resulting in a reduction of approximately 56,800 tCO22e of GHG emissions. Collectively, these initiatives generated 
annual cost savings of approximately ₹176.4 lakhs, and the avoided GHG emissions is 64,467 tCO2e strengthened energy 
resilience, and supported alignment with statutory disclosures and ESG reporting requirements under BRSR, GRI, and global 
rating frameworks.
	
The Gagillapur unit was the major contributor to energy and emissions performance through a combination of renewable energy 
adoption and system efficiency improvements. Key initiatives included rooftop solar generation of 1,203 MWh, procurement of 
7,286 MWh renewable electricity through PPA, replacement of conventional AHU blowers with energy efficient EC+ blowers, 
installation of a high efficiency air compressor, and compressed air pressure optimization. These measures resulted in energy 
savings of 1,548,078 kWh, GHG reduction of 1,099 tCO2e from efficiency initiatives and 5,885 tCO2e from renewable electricity, 
along with annual cost savings of ₹111.6 lakhs.

Business Overview and Operational Performance
Granules India Limited operates a vertically integrated 
pharmaceutical business spanning Active Pharmaceutical 
Ingredients (APIs), Pharmaceutical Formulation Intermediates 
(PFIs), Finished Dosages (FDs) and peptide/CDMO operations. 
The Company continues to strengthen its formulations-
led business model while leveraging backward integration, 
manufacturing scale and operational efficiency to enhance 
supply reliability and cost competitiveness. During FY 2025-
26, Finished Dosages remained the largest revenue contributor, 
accounting for 74% of total revenues, followed by APIs at 13%, 
PFIs at 10% and the emerging peptide/CDMO business at 3%.
Operational performance strengthened during the year, 
supported by robust growth in finished dosage sales across 
regulated markets, particularly North America and Europe. 
Growth was driven by increased demand from existing 
customers, new product launches and the continued expansion 
of the Complex Generics portfolio, including controlled 
substances and ADHD products in the US market. Europe 
also emerged as a strong growth contributor during the year, 
reflecting the Company’s expanding international presence and 
diversified revenue base.
Granules continued to strengthen its manufacturing and supply 
chain capabilities through capacity expansion at the Genome 
Valley formulation facility, enhancing supply flexibility and 
supporting future launches in regulated markets. The Company 
also continued investing in differentiated growth platforms, 
including complex generics, oncology products, peptide 
therapeutics and CDMO capabilities under its Ascelis initiative, 
supporting its transition towards a more value-driven and 
innovation-focused portfolio.
Financial and Segment Performance
Granules India delivered a strong financial and operational 
performance in FY 2025-26, supported by robust growth in 
Finished Dosages, improving product mix and increasing 
contribution from Complex Generics and peptide/CDMO 
operations. Consolidated revenue increased by 20% year-on-
year to ₹53,656 million, while EBITDA grew by 25% to ₹11,851 
million, with EBITDA margins improving to 22.1%. Profit after 
tax increased by 19% to ₹5,950 million despite continued 
investments in R&D, compliance and future growth platforms. 
Gross margins improved significantly to 65.0%, reflecting 
favourable portfolio transformation and operational efficiencies.

R&D and Innovation
Granules continued to strengthen research and development 
as a key driver of long-term growth, portfolio transformation 
and differentiated product development. During FY 2025-26, 
the Company invested ₹2,853 Mn towards R&D, representing 
5.3% of revenues, with a strong focus on complex generics, 
CNS/ADHD therapies, oncology, MUPS and other high-barrier 
formulations. These investments support the Company’s 
strategic transition from a volume-led model towards a value-
driven portfolio with increasing contribution from Complex 
Generics products.
The Company’s global R&D network spans facilities in 
Hyderabad (Genome Valley and Pragathi Nagar), Pune and 
international research capabilities, supported by a team of 
scientists working across APIs, formulations and peptide 
research. During FY 2025-26, Granules filed 6 U.S. ANDAs, 3 
EU dossiers, 1 Canadian dossier and 15 filings across various 
regions, along with 6 U.S. DMFs and 10 additional DMF 
filings globally. Complex generics continued to account for a 
meaningful share of filings, reinforcing the Company’s focus on 
sustainable and differentiated growth opportunities, including 
potential first-to-file launches.
Granules also continued expanding its capabilities in peptides 
and specialty therapeutics through Ascelis Peptides, integrating 
the scientific expertise of Senn Chemicals AG with its global 
development platform. During the year, the peptide CDMO 
platform achieved positive EBITDA in Q4FY 2025-26, while 
the Company further strengthened its peptide development 
ecosystem 
through 
its 
operational 
peptide 
Centre 
of 
Excellence at IIT Hyderabad and planned expansion of peptide 
intermediates and API capabilities in India. These initiatives are 
aligned with the Company’s long-term innovation strategy and 
future growth objectives.
Quality and Compliance
Quality and regulatory compliance remain integral to Granules’ 
operations and long-term competitiveness. During the year, 
the Company continued to strengthen its quality systems and 
governance frameworks across manufacturing facilities to 
ensure alignment with global regulatory expectations.
Granules advanced remediation efforts at the Gagillapur 
Finished Dosage facility, implementing corrective and preventive 
actions while strengthening contamination controls and 
enhancing cleaning validation and quality oversight processes 
with guidance from external experts.
The Company also progressed broader quality enhancement 
initiatives 
through 
revised 
procedures, 
strengthened

Granules remains committed to maintaining robust quality

Sustainability and ESG
FY 2025–26 marked another year of significant progress in 
Granules' sustainability journey, with continued advancement 
across climate action, responsible sourcing and ESG 
governance. 
Sustainability 
remains 
integrated 
into 
the 
Company's long-term strategy, supported by measurable 
environmental 
improvements, 
strengthened 
governance 
frameworks and industry-leading external recognition.
During the year, Granules achieved a Gold Rating from EcoVadis, placing the Company among the top 5% of participating companies 
globally (97th percentile). The Company also strengthened its climate leadership by securing an 'A' rating in the 2025 CDP Climate 
Change assessment, advancing from a 'B' rating in the previous year, while receiving inaugural ratings of 'B' for Water Security and 
'B-' for Forests. Granules' near-term, long-term and Net Zero (2050 or sooner) emissions reduction targets continue to be validated 
by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), reaffirming alignment with the 1.5°C pathway. ESG performance was further reinforced 
through an improved S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment score of 62/100, an MSCI 'BB' rating, and becoming a signatory to 
the UN Women's Empowerment Principles.
The Company also strengthened sustainability across its value chain through an enhanced Supplier Sustainability Programme, 
engaging suppliers representing approximately 80% of procurement spend on climate disclosures, renewable energy adoption 
and emissions management. Granules was recognised on the CDP Supplier Engagement Assessment 2025 A-List, received Sedex 
Supplier Plus recognition and won the Sustainability Award at Haleon's Winning Together – Supplier Summit 2026, reflecting 
continued progress in responsible sourcing and supply chain sustainability. Operationally, the Company achieved a 32% reduction 
in Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, increased the share of renewable electricity to 69%, recycled 44% of wastewater, and directed 
80% of hazardous waste for co-processing, reinforcing its commitment to resource efficiency and low-carbon manufacturing.

Outlook
Granules continues to bolster its position in regulated pharmaceutical markets through the convergence of portfolio expansion, 
operational scale and innovation-led growth. The Finished Dosage segment is expected to remain a crucial growth driver, buoyed

for DCDA production. However, it is in the process of improving 
the Technology to further optimise on cost of Production

DCDA production.

manufacturing process technology for para-aminophenol (PAP) 
first time in the country and is in the process of executing 
a pilot plant to enable decarbonisation of Paracetamol 
production. Efforts are also underway to adopt green energy 
and green molecule manufacturing technologies aimed at 
reducing the overall carbon footprint and achieving net-zero 
emissions by 2050.

ENTERPRISE RISK MANAGEMENT:

set out in the corporate governance report.
The Risk Management Committee has been entrusted with the 
responsibility to:

management framework; 
(b)	
oversee all the risks that the organization faces such as 
financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability (particularly,

other risk as may be determined by the Committee;

risks associated with the business of the Company.

INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS:
Internal financial controls are an integrated part of the risk 
management process, addressing financial and financial 
reporting risks. The internal financial controls have been 
documented, digitized and embedded in the business 
processes. An assurance of the effectiveness of internal financial 
controls is obtained through management reviews, control 
self-assessment, continuous monitoring by functional experts 
as well as testing of the internal financial control systems by 
external consultants on behalf of the management at least 
once a year. We believe that these systems provide reasonable 
assurance that our internal financial controls are designed 
effectively and are operating as intended.
INTERNAL AUDIT AND CONTROLS:
The Company continues to engage M/s. Dhanunjaya & Haranath, 
Chartered Accountants as its internal auditors. During the 
year, the Company continued to implement its suggestions 
and recommendations to improve internal controls. Their 
scope of work includes a review of the operational efficiency, 
the effectiveness of systems & processes, compliance and 
assessing the robustness of the internal control systems in all 
areas of operations and the financial closure process. Internal 
auditor’s findings are discussed and suitable corrective actions 
are taken as per the directions of the Audit Committee on an 
ongoing basis to improve the performance of the Company.

PARTICULARS OF CONSERVATION OF ENERGY
During FY 2025–26, Granules India Limited undertook focused 
energy conservation, efficiency improvement, and renewable 
energy initiatives across its manufacturing sites, delivering 
measurable environmental and financial benefits. The Company 
achieved total energy savings of 2,309,552 kWh, resulting 
in a GHG emission reduction of 1,640 tCO2e through energy 
efficiency measures. Further, increased adoption of renewable 
electricity contributed to an additional 6,027 tCO2e reduction 
in Scope 2 emissions. Additionally, for offsetting emissions, 
Granules procured 80,000 MWh of I-RECs for its API, FD, 
and R&D units, resulting in a reduction of approximately 
56,800 tCO2e of GHG emissions. Collectively, these initiatives 
generated annual cost savings of approximately ₹176.4 lakhs, 
and the avoided GHG emissions is 64,467 tCO2e strengthened 
energy resilience, and supported alignment with statutory 
disclosures and ESG reporting requirements under BRSR, GRI, 
and global rating frameworks.
The Gagillapur unit was the major contributor to energy and 
emissions performance through a combination of renewable 
energy adoption and system efficiency improvements. Key 
initiatives included rooftop solar generation of 1,203 MWh, 
procurement of 7,286 MWh renewable electricity through PPA, 
replacement of conventional AHU blowers with energy efficient 
EC+ blowers, installation of a high efficiency air compressor, 
and compressed air pressure optimization. These measures 
resulted in energy savings of 1,548,078 kWh, GHG reduction 
of 1,099 tCO2e from efficiency initiatives and 5,885 tCO2e 
from renewable electricity, along with annual cost savings 
of ₹111.6 lakhs.
At the Bonthapally unit, energy optimization efforts focused 
on HVAC systems, utilities, and process efficiency. Key 
measures included replacement of AHU blowers with energy 
efficient Aeronaut blowers, interlocking of chillers and RT 
pumps, installation of temperature controllers in cleanroom 
AHUs, deployment of IRIS controllers for air compressors, and 
installation of an auto tube cleaning system for refrigeration 
units. These initiatives delivered energy savings of 758,830 
kWh, corresponding to a GHG reduction of 538.7 tCO2e, and 
annual cost savings of ₹64.6 lakhs.
Energy conservation initiatives at the Parawada unit-IV included 
replacement of conventional street lighting with energy efficient 
bollard lights, adoption of BLDC motors for canteen sealing 
fans, and automation of capacitor banks to achieve unity power 
factor. These measures resulted in energy savings of 2,644 kWh, 
GHG reduction of 2 tCO2e, and annual cost savings of ₹0.5 lakhs.
These initiatives underscore the Company’s commitment 
to sustainability through operational excellence, renewable 
energy adoption, and continuous improvement in energy 
use, all aligned with its long-term Net Zero ambitions and 
science-based targets.

integrated pharmaceutical organization. We further advanced 
our strategic transformation from a leading supplier of APIs 
and PFI to a fully integrated manufacturer of finished dosage

scalable manufacturing processes that meet global standards. 
Backed by a strong foundation of experienced scientific talent 
and an innovation‑driven culture, R&D remains the central 
engine driving execution momentum and long‑term growth. In 
parallel, we enhanced our research capabilities and broadened 
our product portfolio to address emerging opportunities across 
key global markets. Our integrated product, process and market 
led strategy provides a clear competitive advantage positioning 
us as a differentiated partner offering both drug substance and 
drug product solutions and reinforcing our long‑term global 
growth ambitions.
2025- 26 – Highlights
In the API division, we filed a total of 47 (6 in FY 25-26) U.S. 
Drug Master Files (“USDMFs”) across several therapeutic 
categories with the United States Food and Drug Administration 
(“U.S. FDA”) in the United States, 21 (Certificates of Suitability 
(“CEPs”) with the European Directorate for the Quality of 
Medicines (“EDQM”) and 10 (1 in FY 25-26) European Drug 
Master Files (“EDMFs”) in Europe, 12 (2 in FY 25-26) Korean 
Drug Master files, 7 China Master Files, 5 CADIFA Files in Brazil 
along with other regulatory filings in key regulated markets to 
support potential customers for ANDA and dossier filings.
 
 
As part of our vertical integration strategy, we intend to file 
ANDAs for several of these APIs to forward integrate into FDFs.
 
 
As part of expanding our oncology portfolio we have 
completed development of 3 new products.
 
 
As part of our control substances expansion, we have 
developed 2 new APIs towards vertical integration to FD. The 
products are developed in our controlled substances lab and 
validated in unit IV facility. We have filed US DMF of one of the 
control substance products which is developed in our R & D 
and validated at our CMO partner, USA. 
 
 
As part of the green initiative, the Bio-catalysis group which is 
actively working on the development and scale up of enzymes 
for APIs and intermediates. The team has successfully 
developed immobilization technology towards development 
of re-usable biocatalyst. 
 
 
A dedicated fermentation group is created for the development 
of Peptides and the development of enzymes for Biocatalysis. 
This group has successfully developed optimized and scaled 
up an enzyme for one of the API intermediates. Using the 
same enzyme we have successfully completed validation of 
the product in our unit-V facility. 
 
 
To strengthen our capabilities in crystal morphology studies, 
and particle engineering, we have established centre of 
excellence at IIT Hyderabad. This group is dedicated for 
developing novel polymorphic form of APIs and addressing 
any particle challenges in our APIs. 
 
 
Ascelis Peptides Private Limited, the CDMO arm of Granules 
is working in close collaboration with Senn Chemicals AG,

Hyderabad, whose primary focus being peptide development.
